title: tree-shaking
description: Learn about tree-shaking. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Tree shaking is a build optimization technique that eliminates dead code from your bundles. It analyzes the dependency graph and removes exports that are never imported, reducing bundle size without changing functionality.

Tree shaking relies on ES modules (ESM) because they have a static structure that allows build tools to analyze dependencies at build time. CommonJS modules cannot be tree-shaken because their dependencies are determined at runtime.

data.title: Tree Shaking Process

data.text: Tree shaking only works with ES modules. CommonJS (require/module.exports) cannot be tree-shaken because dependencies are determined dynamically at runtime.

data.title: Module Format Comparison
data.content: Why ESM enables tree shaking but CommonJS doesn't.

data.text: Modern bundlers like Webpack, Rollup, and Vite have tree shaking enabled by default in production mode. However, you may need to configure it for optimal results.

data.title: Webpack Tree Shaking Configuration
data.content: Configure webpack for optimal tree shaking.

data.text: Modules with side effects (code that affects global state when imported) cannot be safely tree-shaken. You can mark modules as side-effect-free using the sideEffects field in package.json.
When developing libraries, structure your code to maximize tree shaking for consumers. Use ESM exports, avoid side effects, and prefer named exports over default exports.

data.title: Tree-Shakeable Library Structure
data.content: Design libraries for optimal tree shaking.

data.text: Use webpack-bundle-analyzer or similar tools to verify that tree shaking is working correctly. Look for unused exports that are still being included in your bundles.

data.title: Webpack Bundle Analyzer
data.content: Visualize what's included in your bundles.

data.title: Class Methods and Tree Shaking
data.text: Unused class methods are harder to eliminate than standalone functions. Consider using standalone functions when possible for better tree shaking.

data.title: Functions vs Classes for Tree Shaking
data.content: Functions are more tree-shakeable than classes.

data.text: Modern bundlers support advanced tree shaking patterns like property access tree shaking, which can eliminate unused object properties and methods.

data.title: Property Access Tree Shaking
data.content: Webpack can eliminate unused object properties.
